Dear old nurse, Mrs. Crockett, eminently a nurse of the old school, who had nursed and brought up almost every Kennedy that ever was born, used to wear the most impossible “mobcaps, ” which she manufactured herself on an article called a “dummy, ” a thing rather the shape of a skull, upon which we children looked with the greatest reverence.

“I know — in a grubby street of yellow brick houses — soiled women in mobcaps, dirty children, the odour of boiling cabbage — ” She bent her head, while her lovely shoulders gave a shudder of repulsion.
